q: Which type of lenes are used in telescope? (2026)
e: Convex lenses are used in astronomical telescopes to converge light rays and form magnified images.

q: Which part of the eye functions similarly to the diaphragm in a camera, controlling the amount of light that enters the eye? (2025)
e: The iris regulates the size of the pupil, controlling the amount of light entering the eye, similar to the diaphragm in a camera.

q: What does monochromatic light refer to? (2024)
a: Light of a single wavelength or colour
e: Monochromatic light refers to light consisting of a single wavelength or color.

q: ________ is the defect of vision in which distant objects are seen clearly, but objects near-by are blurry. (2026)
e: Farsightedness (hyperopia) is a vision defect where distant objects are clearly visible, but nearby objects appear blurry.

q: A microscope uses lenses to make ________ images of objects. (2025)
e: A microscope uses convex lenses to produce enlarged images of tiny objects.

q: What type of lens is used as an eyepiece to produce an erect final image in terrestrial telescope? (2024)
e: A terrestrial telescope uses a concave lens as an eyepiece to produce an upright (erect) final image.

q: A ________ controls the time during which light enters the camera through the lens. (2025)
e: The shutter controls the exposure duration during which light reaches the photographic surface.

q: The core of a fibre-optic cable is made of ________. (2025)
e: The core of a fiber-optic cable is made of thin strands of glass or transparent material to transmit light signals.

q: When taking a photograph in bright light a ________ f-number must be used. (2025)
e: A larger f-number reduces the aperture size, restricting light entry to prevent overexposure in bright conditions.

q: The yellow spot which is the most light-sensitive spot is ________. (2025)
e: The yellow spot (fovea centralis) is located on the retina and contains the highest density of photoreceptor cells.

q: Which part of the human eye is responsible for adjusting the focus of light to form a clear image on the retina? (2025)
e: The eye lens changes its curvature to adjust focal distance and focus light sharply on the retina.

q: Which color of light is more sensitive to the human eye? (2025)
e: The human eye is naturally most sensitive to green light under daylight conditions.

q: What principle is utilized in a compound microscope to achieve high magnification? (2025)
a: Refraction of light through a convex lens
e: A compound microscope uses successive refraction of light through objective and eyepiece convex lenses to magnify objects.

q: What is the SI unit of illuminance? (2025)
e: Lux (lx) is the SI unit of illuminance, representing luminous flux per unit area.

q: Which of the following does not make use of total internal reflection? (2025)
e: An oscilloscope operates via electron beams on a phosphor screen, whereas endoscopes and optical fibers use total internal reflection.

q: A microscope uses lenses to make ________ images of objects. (2025)
e: Lenses in a microscope bend light rays to create significantly enlarged images of small objects.

q: The ________ which is the colored portion of the eye controls the amount of light energy entering the eye. (2025)
e: The iris is the colored ring of muscle that contracts or expands to regulate light entry through the pupil.

q: Which of the following is the SI basic unit of luminous intensity? (2025)
e: Candela (cd) is the base SI unit measuring the luminous intensity of a light source.

q: When near objects are viewed, the ciliary muscles contract and the eyelens becomes ________. (2025)
e: When focusing on near objects, ciliary muscle contraction makes the eye lens more convex to increase its refractive power.

q: Monochromatic light means that it has a ________ wavelength. (2025)
e: Monochromatic light consists of light rays of a single wavelength.

q: The film consists of a thin layer of chemical compounds of ________. (2025)
e: Photographic film uses light-sensitive silver compounds (such as silver halides) to record images.

q: ________ is a defect of vision in which near objects are seen clearly, but objects far away are blurry. (2026)
e: Nearsightedness (myopia) is a condition where near objects appear sharp while distant objects appear blurred.

q: Which wavelength corresponds to the maximum sensitivity of the human eye under day light? (2026)
e: In daylight conditions (photopic vision), human eye sensitivity peaks at 555 nm in the green spectrum.

q: What is the main function of the cladding in an optical fibre? (2026)
a: To protect the core from external damage
To increase the core's refractive index
To provide a lower refractive index to cause total internal reflection in the core
e: The cladding has a lower refractive index than the core, allowing light signals to undergo total internal reflection inside the core.
